newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Coca-Cola to build Uzbek plant in $100 million investment.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola to build Uzbek plant in $100 million investment.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Co. said Friday it will spend $50 million to build a bottling plant in Tashkent as part of a $100 million investment in the former Soviet republic of Uzbekistan.

"Coca Cola will be investing $100 million over the next 18 months in Uzbekistan to further develop our local production and distribution," John Sheppard, president of Coca-Cola East Central Europe, told a news conference in Tashkent, the republic's capital.
Construction of the bottling plant will begin next month, Sheppard said.
Sheppard said the investment was part of a two-year investment plan for the former Soviet republics of the Caucasus and Central Asia totalling $200 million.
On Friday Coca-Cola opened a $10 million bottling plant in Namangan, Uzbekistan, its third facility in the largely desert nation of 23 million.
The Tashkent operation, to be named Coca-Cola Bottlers Tashkent Ltd, will be owned by a joint venture comprising Coca-Cola Export Corp., Uzbekistan's Roz Group and state-owned Uzpisheprom.
